decisions.question: Where does topics.yaml live and what does it generate: one Dart file per domain (Guide C.3's auth_topics.dart), one library per schema file, or one schema file per domain?

options.label: one library per schema file at lib/topics.yaml to lib/topics.g.dart
options.consequence: build_runner can express it (outputs are fixed by the input path); Spec §4.5's single multi-domain file stays; app code still reads AuthTopics.state; diverges from Guide C.3's per-domain file name

options.label: one file per domain from one schema file
options.consequence: matches Guide C.3, but no build_runner builder can name outputs after domains read from inside the input, so build_runner and the command could not write the same files (ADR-002 item 8)

options.label: one schema file per domain ({domain}.topics.yaml to {domain}_topics.dart)
options.consequence: build_runner can express it, but splits Spec §4.5's single source of truth, and two files in different directories could declare one domain

decisions.chosen: one library per schema file at lib/topics.yaml to lib/topics.g.dart
decisions.why: Spec §4.5 has one topics.yaml with many domains, Guide C.2 asks for build_runner integration, and ADR-002 item 8 requires the builder and the command to write identical bytes; only one output per input satisfies all three. The ^lib/topics.yaml build extension was run on the pinned build 4.0.11 and build_runner 2.16.1 (T5): it applies to lib/topics.yaml only and writes the command's bytes. Guide C.3's per-domain file is informative; marked for upstreaming.

decisions.question: What does topics.yaml's initial hold? Spec §4.5's example values (Initializing, empty) are not Dart.

options.label: a Dart expression string, or a YAML number, boolean or null written as the Dart literal
options.consequence: unambiguous and total: any initial value the topic-model constructors accept can be written; the Spec's example values become identifiers that must be in scope; Dart-specific

options.label: a token resolved against the type (Initializing as AuthState.initializing)
options.consequence: reads like the Spec's example and is platform-neutral, but the generator cannot tell a constructor from a static field or an enum value without resolving types, so the output would not compile reliably

options.label: a Dart expression string only
options.consequence: simplest rule, but initial: 0 and initial: false, the natural YAML, would be rejected

decisions.chosen: a Dart expression string, or a YAML number, boolean or null written as the Dart literal
decisions.why: The generator is a pure function over YAML with no type resolution, so only an expression it copies verbatim always compiles when the author's expression does. Accepting number, boolean and null literals keeps the natural YAML for primitive topics; probe/yaml_facts.out.txt shows how package:yaml 3.1.4 types each scalar, including that an empty value is null and .inf is a non-finite double, which R4 rejects. The Spec's schema is shared across platforms and says nothing about what initial holds; marked for upstreaming. Signal that would change it: a second platform port, which would need a platform-neutral initial value form.

decisions.question: How does a topics document say which Dart libraries declare its types?

options.label: per-domain dart.imports list
options.consequence: imports travel with the domain a team owns; the Dart-only key is namespaced, so the schema can stay every platform's source

options.label: top-level imports list
options.consequence: simpler, but the name would be claimed by Dart for every later platform, and imports detach from the domains that need them

options.label: builder options in build.yaml plus command arguments
options.consequence: keeps the YAML platform-neutral, but two configuration sources would have to agree for the builder and the command to write identical bytes

decisions.why: Spec §4.5 and Guide C.3 make the schema file the single source for every platform's generator; a namespaced key keeps that, and one source keeps ADR-002 item 8's identical bytes. No evidence distinguishes per-domain from top-level beyond ownership: domains have owners (Spec Appendix A.9).

decisions.question: Does the topics document reject unknown keys, or ignore them?

options.label: closed: every unknown key is an error
options.consequence: a misspelled sensitve: true fails instead of silently leaving a sensitive topic unflagged; a later key is a compatible addition for the generator

options.label: open: unknown keys ignored
options.consequence: a later platform's keys pass unchanged, but a typo in sensitive or tracing is silent

decisions.chosen: closed: every unknown key is an error
decisions.why: Spec §9.2 makes the sensitive flag the privacy gate; a silently ignored misspelling would publish a sensitive topic to every observer. topology-ir@v1's schema is closed for the same kind of reason.

decisions.question: Does the file contract also carry a JSON Schema for topics.yaml with valid/ and invalid/ cases, and in which syntax are the cases written?

options.label: schema with JSON-syntax cases, plus rejected/ YAML for the generator-only rules
options.consequence: the format is machine-checkable and editor-usable; the replay tool's schema set runs it with no YAML parser; rules JSON Schema cannot state (repeated keys, collisions, reserved words, non-finite numbers) get YAML inputs the producer's gates use

options.label: schema with YAML cases
options.consequence: cases read like real topics.yaml, but nidana_contract_check would need package:yaml, a dependency outside ADR-002's table that nidana.model would have to add

options.label: no schema, the file replay only
options.consequence: fewer artifacts, but the accepted format would be stated only in prose and one input tree, and invalid inputs would have no fixture at all

decisions.chosen: schema with JSON-syntax cases, plus rejected/ YAML for the generator-only rules
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 6 gives a file contract one input tree, which cannot show what is rejected; a schema set with invalid cases is the only executable form ADR-001 has for that (item 5). JSON is YAML 1.2, so the cases are also generator inputs (T8: all 4 valid accepted, all 53 invalid rejected with exit 1). The schema compiled and classified every case as marked under package:json_schema 5.2.2 and strict Ajv 8.17.1 (T6, T7); its variant rules were restructured from not/required to properties: false so strict Ajv compiles it.

decisions.question: What exact Dart shape does a generated registry member take?

options.label: static final with the type written on the field and the constructor, non-default arguments only, no collections
options.consequence: one form for every variant; nothing inferred, so topic-model@v1's MultiWriterTopic LUB change cannot reach generated code; minimal arguments

options.label: static const for event and replay topics, static final for state topics
options.consequence: event and replay topics usable in const contexts, at the cost of two forms; state topics cannot be const because initial is an arbitrary expression

options.label: inferred field types as Guide C.3 writes them (static final state = StateTopic<AuthState>(...))
options.consequence: shorter, but leaves the field type to inference, which S10's note asks generated code to avoid

decisions.chosen: static final with the type written on the field and the constructor, non-default arguments only, no collections
decisions.why: topic-model@v1 allows static const or static final in an abstract final class; Guide C.3 shows static final; topics compare by value (topic-model@v1 G7), so const identity buys nothing a registry needs. The S10 note concerns inferred collection element types; generating no collection and writing every type out removes inference altogether. The generated library analyzed clean under lints/recommended, strict modes and --fatal-infos (T4).

decisions.question: How are class and member names derived, and what happens when a key cannot become a Dart identifier?

options.label: camel-case derivation, and reject collisions, reserved words and Object member names (R2, R3)
options.consequence: the identifier always reads as the key; a bad key is an error the author fixes once

options.label: camel-case derivation with mangling (switch to switch_, a numeric suffix on collision)
options.consequence: never rejects, but names stop being predictable from the key, and the mangled form trips non_constant_identifier_names

decisions.chosen: camel-case derivation, and reject collisions, reserved words and Object member names (R2, R3)
decisions.why: probe/names/output.txt compiled a static member under each of 70 candidate names: exactly the 33 reserved words and hashCode, runtimeType, toString, noSuchMethod fail; every built-in and contextual identifier compiles. Rejecting exactly that set is the smallest rule under which every accepted document generates compiling code.

decisions.question: How is a description rendered into a doc comment and the catalog?

options.label: Markdown, with < and > outside code spans backslash-escaped
options.consequence: authors keep code spans; raw angle brackets never read as HTML, so the library stays clean under --fatal-infos and the catalog carries no HTML

options.label: Markdown verbatim
options.consequence: a description such as 'emits List<int>' trips unintended_html_in_doc_comment, an INFO that fails every --fatal-infos gate

options.label: plain text, every Markdown character escaped
options.consequence: always safe, but code spans the author writes would show their backticks

decisions.chosen: Markdown, with < and > outside code spans backslash-escaped
decisions.why: probe/doc/output.txt: the lint reports only the raw <int>; a code span, a backslash escape, a comparison with spaces and an autolink pass. Escaping outside code spans keeps the author's Markdown and the gate clean.

decisions.question: What does the topic catalog topics.md contain and how are graph topics matched to document topics?

options.label: per-domain and per-topic sections with property tables, readers and writers from the graph matched by name, plus topology, claim and outside-topic sections
options.consequence: covers Spec Appendix A.9's list (types, sensitivity, owners, readers and writers with scopes); hand-written registries' topics appear from the graph

options.label: one flat table of topics
options.consequence: compact, but descriptions and reader lists do not fit table cells

decisions.chosen: per-domain and per-topic sections with property tables, readers and writers from the graph matched by name, plus topology, claim and outside-topic sections
decisions.why: Spec Appendix A.9 and Guide §5.2 item 5 list what a catalog shows, including the topologies that read and write each topic and their scopes; Guide C.3 asks for cross-references. Matching by name, not type, because a graph's TopicRef.typeName is the runtime rendering while the document holds the author's text (topology-ir@v1). No evidence beyond the Spec's list decides the layout.

decisions.question: How does the build-time topology graph page (Guide C.4) render the graph?

options.label: static HTML embedding topology-ir@v1's Mermaid rendering, Mermaid 11.12.0 loaded from jsDelivr when opened
options.consequence: small, byte-stable page; reuses a rendering topology-ir@v1 already pins; needs network to draw, and shows the readable diagram text offline

options.label: inline the Mermaid library into every page
options.consequence: renders offline, but each generated page carries megabytes of third-party code

options.label: SVG laid out at build time
options.consequence: renders offline with no script, but needs Graphviz or a layout engine in the build, which is global tooling

decisions.chosen: static HTML embedding topology-ir@v1's Mermaid rendering, Mermaid 11.12.0 loaded from jsDelivr when opened
decisions.why: The build itself needs no network and no global tool; the page's pre text equals topology-ir@v1's render/checkout.mmd golden byte for byte after jsdom's HTML parsing, and Mermaid 11.12.0 parses it (T7). A careful engineer would ask whether the owner's docs must render offline (an external network resource at view time); the signal that would change it is that requirement.

decisions.question: Which commands does nidana_dart_codegen expose for this contract, with which arguments and exit codes?

options.label: generate [--graph <graph>] <topics> <output> (pure) and catalog <package>... <output> (runs topology code), exit 0, 1 for rejected input, 2 for usage
options.consequence: the replayable part is a pure function of two files; the graph document is the seam between the catalog run and the documents; one exit-code convention for both

options.label: one command reading an app package and writing everything
options.consequence: one invocation, but nothing is replayable until OQ-T1's mechanism exists, and the docs could not be generated from a graph built elsewhere

decisions.chosen: generate [--graph <graph>] <topics> <output> (pure) and catalog <package>... <output> (runs topology code), exit 0, 1 for rejected input, 2 for usage
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 6 needs a generator command over an input tree; ADR-002 item 8 names a generator command and leaves names, arguments and exit codes to this contract; Spec §6.5's Catalog.scanTopologies takes a list of packages. The stand-in's exit codes held for every case (T8, T9, T11); T11 first exited 255 because head closed the pipe, an artifact of the script, fixed by capturing to a file.

decisions.question: Must this contract fix any part of OQ-T1 (how Catalog.scanTopologies obtains every TopologyDefinition without reflection)?

options.label: fix the output and the definitions' origin only: topology-graph.json holds buildDefinition() of the registered topologies, recorded on the VM unobfuscated; leave registration to the decomposition
options.consequence: consumers can mock against a fixed document; the decomposition keeps every discovery mechanism; catalog's guarantees are not executable here until it picks one

options.label: also fix the registration form now (for example an explicit list the app writes)
options.consequence: catalog would get a replay case, but this step would decide nidana.tooling's open question before its decomposition and before nidana-checks@v1, which shares the scan

options.label: fix nothing about the catalog
options.consequence: topology-ir@v1's Boundary assigns topology-graph.json's path and generator to this contract, which would stay unnamed

decisions.chosen: fix the output and the definitions' origin only: topology-graph.json holds buildDefinition() of the registered topologies, recorded on the VM unobfuscated; leave registration to the decomposition
decisions.why: Spec §6.5 states the catalog instantiates topology classes and calls buildDefinition(), so the static and runtime graphs are structurally identical; topology-ir@v1 assigns this contract the path and generator and requires a VM run without --obfuscate. How topologies are found, how constructor arguments are supplied, and how Flutter-importing libraries load are mechanism, owned by the decomposition (OQ-T1 Waits on). probe/flutter-vm shows dart run cannot load a library that imports Flutter (dart:ui missing) while flutter test can, which the decomposition must handle.

decisions.question: Does topology-graph.json hold shell claims, and from where?

options.label: yes, the claims nidana-checks@v1's workspace scan resolves; unresolvable ones left out with a warning
options.consequence: the published graph is the one the single-writer and scope checks analyze; the claim recognizer is shared with S16

options.label: topologies only
options.consequence: simpler catalog, but topology-ir@v1 defines the catalog's graph with claims, and shell-owned state topics would show no writer

decisions.chosen: yes, the claims nidana-checks@v1's workspace scan resolves; unresolvable ones left out with a warning
decisions.why: Spec §3.11: the same scan feeds the topology graph generator, where publisher claims appear as source nodes; topology-ir@v1 Refinement 3 builds the catalog's graph from every topology and claim the workspace declares; Spec §3.11 leaves unresolvable write sets to the runtime with a warning.

decisions.question: One input/expected pair, as ADR-001 item 6 reads, or several cases?

options.label: one input/expected pair, with a graph, covering every feature in one document
options.consequence: matches ADR-001 item 6 literally, so the replay tool needs nothing new; the no-graph and failure behaviors are not executable and fall to nidana.tooling's gates

options.label: case subdirectories input/{case}/ and expected/{case}/
options.consequence: more behaviors replayable, but the replay tool would implement a layout ADR-001 does not state

decisions.chosen: one input/expected pair, with a graph, covering every feature in one document
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 6 names one command over input/ compared with expected/, while item 7 gives cli contracts per-case directories; writing a layout the replay tool's author would not find in ADR-001 risks a structure failure at the first replay. Signal that would change it: an ADR-001 amendment adding cases and an expected exit code to file contracts, which would make G2, G14 and G19 executable.

decisions.question: Does the generator format its Dart itself, given the replay formats anyway?

options.label: format with package:dart_style at language 3.13
options.consequence: committed registries pass a format check; build_runner and the command format alike; the replay's own format pass is a no-op

options.label: emit unformatted text and rely on the replay's fvm dart format
options.consequence: less code, but a committed lib/topics.g.dart would fail any format check in a gate

decisions.why: ADR-002 lists dart_style among nidana_dart_codegen's dependencies; the stand-in's dart_style 3.1.14 output was unchanged by the SDK's fvm dart format (T1, T2).

decisions.question: Is a domain's owner required?

options.label: required
options.consequence: every catalog row names an owning team; a one-person app writes one owner line per domain

options.label: optional
options.consequence: less friction for small apps, but catalog rows without an owner

decisions.why: Spec Appendix A.9 lists owning teams from the schema's owner field as part of the catalog, and every example in Spec §4.5 and Guide C.3 carries one. A requirement can be relaxed compatibly later; the reverse is breaking.

decisions.question: Which outputs does the build_runner builder write?

options.label: the registry library only
options.consequence: the builder is per input and pure; topics.md and the page, which need the graph, come only from generate

options.label: the registry and topics.md
options.consequence: a catalog without readers and writers next to the source, differing from generate's catalog, which ADR-002 item 8's identical-bytes rule forbids for shared outputs

decisions.why: The catalog's cross references need the graph, which only a catalog run produces; a builder output under lib/ that names topologies would also sit in an importable location, against Spec §4.6 and Guide C.5.

decisions.question: Frontmatter: consumers, external consumers, governance.

options.label: consumers [nidana.integration], three external consumers, Governed by ADR-001 and ADR-002
options.consequence: as the root contract matrix names; ADR-003 does not list this contract

options.label: also list nidana-checks@v1's scan as a consumer
options.consequence: the scan is produced by the same node, so it is not a contract edge

decisions.chosen: consumers [nidana.integration], three external consumers, Governed by ADR-001 and ADR-002
decisions.why: Root contract matrix row topic-codegen@v1; ADR-001 and ADR-002 affects lists include topic-codegen@v1; node ids with phase_ids provisional until reconcile.

experiments.question: Does a stand-in generator over input/ produce exactly expected/ after fvm dart format, does the generated Dart compile against a stand-in nidana_dart_contracts, do build_runner and the command write identical bytes, and do the schema cases validate as marked?
experiments.finding: Yes on every count (output.txt T1 to T13). generate over input/ reproduced expected/ byte for byte with and without fvm dart format and from absolute paths (T1 to T3); the library analyzed clean in a stand-in app under lints/recommended, strict modes and --fatal-infos (T4); build_runner 2.16.1 with build 4.0.11 applied ^lib/topics.yaml only, wrote the command's bytes, failed on a rejected document and then deleted the stale output (T5); package:json_schema 5.2.2 and strict Ajv 8.17.1 classified 4 valid and 53 invalid cases as marked, and input/topics.yaml and the 5 parsable rejected/ documents validate (T6, T7); the generator accepted all valid/, rejected all invalid/ and rejected/ with exit 1 and no output, with file:line:column diagnostics (T8, T9); without a graph it wrote the same registry and a catalog without graph rows (T10); usage errors exit 2, an undecodable graph 1 (T11); the page's pre text equals topology-ir@v1 render/checkout.mmd and Mermaid 11.12.0 parses it (T7).

experiments.question: What does package:yaml 3.1.4 do with repeated keys, several documents, JSON input, mapping order and each scalar kind?
experiments.finding: Repeated key and second document throw YamlException with a span; order is kept; JSON parses; empty value and ~ are null, .inf and .nan non-finite doubles, yes a string, a 20-digit integer a lossy double (yaml_facts.out.txt). Grounds R1 and R4 and the initial-value rendering.

experiments.question: Which doc comment renderings trip unintended_html_in_doc_comment?
experiments.finding: Only a raw <int>; a code span, a backslash escape, a spaced comparison and an autolink are clean (output.txt). Grounds the angle-bracket escape (G16).

experiments.question: Which names can a static member of an abstract final class take?
experiments.finding: Exactly the 33 reserved words and hashCode, runtimeType, toString, noSuchMethod fail; all 36 built-in and contextual identifiers tried compile (output.txt). Grounds R3.

experiments.question: Can a catalog running under dart run load a library that imports Flutter?
experiments.finding: No: dart run fails with 'Dart library dart:ui is not available on this platform' (exit 254); the same library loads under fvm flutter test (T13). A constraint for OQ-T1's mechanism.

notes_for_orchestrator: No existing contract needs a change. topology-ir@v1's Boundary and The JSON form assign topology-graph.json's path and generator here; this contract names them: catalog <package>... <output> writes {output}/topology-graph.json as JsonRenderer of the catalog's graph.

For S16 (nidana-checks@v1): (1) topology-graph.json holds the shell claims 'the workspace scan nidana-checks@v1 defines' resolves (bus.publisher(source, writes:, scope:), and PageScope(writes:) per S14's note), with unresolvable claims left out and warned; S16 must define that recognizer once so catalog and the scan share it (Spec §3.11, ADR-002 item 8). (2) The scan may read topology-graph.json, Guide C.3's 'CI lint manifest', or build the same graph in-process; either way one graph. (3) Generated registries are lib/topics.g.dart: abstract final classes with static final members whose first argument is name: '{domain}.{key}' as a string literal, with explicit types; topic-name uniqueness across registries must read them like hand-written ones, and the raw-string-topic rule must accept these literals (ADR-002 Consequences). (4) catalog exits 1 on two unequal definitions sharing a topologyId; the scan still has to report duplicate ids itself (S08 note). (5) generate and catalog use exit 0 / 1 rejected input / 2 usage; S16 may reuse the convention for the scan command.

For nidana.tooling's decomposition: OQ-T1 is now partly decided by this contract and its row should become PARTIAL citing topic-codegen@v1: the document holds buildDefinition() of every registered topology, recorded on the Dart VM in JIT mode without --obfuscate, plus the scan's claims. Still open there: how topologies are registered (a convention over declarations, an annotation, which would need a declaration in nidana_dart_contracts and so a topology-dsl@v1 amendment, or an app-written list), the build-time configuration for constructor arguments (Spec §6.5), and how Flutter-importing topology libraries load: dart run cannot load dart:ui, flutter test can (probe/flutter-vm, T13). A builder that writes a catalog entry point would join topic-codegen@v1 by amendment as a file layout. The builder and generate must share one pure function; the stand-in in the experiment shows the shape on the pinned build 4.0.11, dart_style 3.1.14 (formatting at language 3.13) and yaml 3.1.4; build_runner deletes the stale lib/topics.g.dart when the builder fails.

For nidana.tooling's phase gates (the eight not-executable guarantees): G2 run the generator over valid/, invalid/ and rejected/; G9 compare unformatted output with fvm dart format's; G10 compile generated output against nidana_dart_contracts with resolvable types; G11 build_test or a build_runner run in a test package compared with generate's bytes; G14 the no-graph run; G19 exit codes and nothing written; G20 and G21 decode and schema-check what catalog writes over fixture topologies.

For nidana.model's replay tool (its first phase): the file set for topic-codegen runs `fvm dart run nidana_dart_codegen:generate --graph {input}/topology-graph.json {input}/topics.yaml {output}` from the workspace root into an empty directory, formats the Dart in {output}, and compares the tree with expected/ including the file set; the schema set runs on this file contract's valid/ and invalid/ (.json); the tool must not analyze expected/topics.g.dart (its imports name a stand-in app) and must tolerate rejected/, which no set reads.

ADR-001 follow-up candidates (an hsdd-adr touch, not blocking): item 3's coverage wording names reject fixtures and behavior cases only, so for file and cli contracts the structure set has to accept coverage by the file replay or recorded invocations as Validation states it ('The file set covers G3 to G8, ...'); item 6 has one input/expected pair and no expected exit code, so a generator's rejection, the no-graph mode and failure exits are not executable (G2, G14, G19); an amendment adding case directories and an exit code per case would make them executable.

For nidana.integration: packages/nidana_integration/lib/topics.yaml and build_runner run in that member; its gate can compare the committed lib/topics.g.dart with generate's output (exercising G11) and analyze the app (G10); NavigationTopics and other hand-written registries appear in topics.md under 'Topics outside topics.yaml'.

Upstream findings (would_upstream) for REPORT.md: Guide C.3's Dart row shows one file per domain, which build_runner cannot produce from one multi-domain schema file (one library per schema file here); Spec §4.5's topics.yaml example does not say what initial holds per platform (a Dart expression here).

would_have_asked: the topology graph page loads Mermaid 11.12.0 from jsDelivr when opened (stop_class external); the owner may want docs that render offline, which would mean inlining the library or a build-time SVG.
